title: Stabilize Microsoft Before Cutover

cta.text: See Micetro with your Microsoft servers

prompt:
Product: BlueCat. Demo: "Stabilize Microsoft Before Cutover".
Start with one welcome step whose title is exactly "Find the Weak Spots in Your Microsoft DHCP and DNS Before You Move Anything" and whose text is exactly: Two domain controllers, one short punch list. Watch BlueCat Micetro find the scopes with no failover partner, protect one, and copy a single-copy DNS zone to a second server, so the new design does not inherit the risk.
Audience: network and DNS engineers and IT leaders evaluating the product. Tone: concise, confident, practical, no hype.
19 screenshots, keep this order, one tooltip per image, calling out the highlighted UI element. Use the text of each numbered tooltip EXACTLY as written; do not rewrite, shorten or merge it. Do not add a closing step or a closing message after the last screenshot; its own tooltip is the end.
1. DLG-DC01 serves 21 scopes. The last column, Failover relationship, says which ones have a partner server. Reading 21 rows by eye does not scale, so use the Quick filter.
2. Type the filter in the Quick filter and only the scopes that already have a failover partner remain: one. Now flip the filter to see the rest.
3. The same filter, reversed, lists the scopes that depend on DC01 alone: 20. That is your punch list. Pick one and give it a partner, starting with a new failover relationship.
4. Failover is managed on the DHCP service, under Admin, Service management. This is Manage failover for DLG-DC01: one relationship exists already. To protect a scope that has none, add a new one. Select Add relationship.
5. Name the new relationship. The mode is Load balance and the primary server is DC01. Next, choose the partner server.
6. DLG-DC02 is the partner. Continue to the options, then the summary.
7. A failover relationship is three short steps: a name, a mode and a partner server. The summary shows all three before anything is saved. Select Add.
8. Micetro asks for a change comment on every write, so each change has a reason on record. Add a short one, then save.
9. The relationship is saved. It has no scopes yet, so next, give it one from the punch list.
10. Filter to one scope from the punch list, 10.10.14.0/24. Open its row menu and choose Add scope to failover.
11. Pick the failover relationship the scope should join. Open the list.
12. Choose the new relationship, then confirm. Micetro creates the matching scope on DC02 for you.
13. The scope now has DC02 as its partner. Run the first filter again: two scopes have a failover partner instead of one.
14. And the punch list is one shorter: 19. That drop is the progress you can report.
15. Zones need the same check. Micetro has no report for zones that live on one server, so compare the two servers side by side. This is DLG-DC01. Select DLG-DC02 next.
16. DLG-DC02 hosts fewer zones. Four zones exist on DC01 only, among them legacy-apps. If DC01 is lost, those zones go with it. Pick one and copy it.
17. Choose DLG-DC02 as the destination. Leave Remove original zone clear: the original stays where it is, so this makes a second copy rather than a move.
18. legacy-apps now lives on both servers.
19. Reconcile compares the Windows registry with the DHCP database for a scope. This one is consistent. If a mismatch exists, Micetro lists it here and Fix repairs it.
